report:
Summary conclusion
- The difference is primarily a change in the model's representation at the first token (position 0) across many layers — i.e., a changed BOS / initial-context bias — not a clearly identifiable semantic domain difference.
- Functionally, that changed residual vector biases continuations toward short, list-like / mapping / echoing or “instructional” snippets (copies, token->token mappings, enumerations, tiny code-like fragments) when injected into an identity prompt.
- I cannot identify a single specific task/objective (e.g., “more safety”, “more legal text”, etc.) from this evidence.

Why
- Location of the signal: The L2 norms show almost all of the difference concentrated on position 0 across layers (very large pos0 magnitudes from middle to late layers, much smaller at pos1+). That pattern looks like a change in how the two checkpoints treat the beginning-of-sequence token / initial context rather than a distributed change tied to later-token processing.
- Patchscope behavior: Injecting the difference vector at various layers into an identity prompt produces outputs that are repeatedly:
  - small mappings (e.g. "100 -> 0", "bits -> 1"), echoing/identity lines ("hello -> hello", "me -> me"), enumerations/lists, and short code-like or prompt-like fragments.
  - those continuations are stylistic/structural (formatting, copying, transform tasks) rather than consistently about a single topical domain.
  This supports the interpretation that the difference encodes a bias toward an “instructional/list/mapping/echo” generation mode.
- Logit-lens tokens: The top tokens the difference vectors point to are varied across layers (nouns like "bottle", "wings", author/title tokens, and later words like "tragic", "law", "surgeon", "blitz", "coming"). The vocabulary signals are noisy and mixed, not pointing to one clear semantic objective; they are consistent with a vector that biases early-token logits toward many high-frequency content tokens (which, combined with the positional pattern, changes the model’s initial continuation style).

Caveats / what I cannot say
- I cannot confidently name a specific downstream objective the checkpoints were trained on (e.g., “more copy-paste behavior” as an explicit fine-tune). The evidence supports a representational/bias difference at position 0 and a functional effect on the style of continuations, but not a single labelled domain or concrete training target.
- The exact mechanism (different learned BOS embedding vs. different early-layer residual paths vs. an inserted learned prompt) cannot be distinguished from this data alone; all are consistent with a changed initial-context signal.
